blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Children’s rights advocates on Thursday welcomed the House of Representatives’ approval of the substitute bill for the Children’s Social Media and Online Gaming Safety Act but raised concerns over provisions requiring parental consent for children to access social media and restricting short-form videos. The House Committee on Welfare of Children approved the substitute bill on Sept. 7, consolidating 41 measures. The proposed legislation seeks to set minimum age requirements, strengthen parental oversight and impose stronger safety standards on social media and online gaming platforms.
